problem: The note 'with reference electrode' is attached to the p-silicon substrate. The text and the figure caption both put the reference electrode in the sample electrolyte above the gate. A student reading the stack will think the Ag/AgCl electrode sits inside the silicon.
fix: Change that item to {'label': 'p-silicon substrate', 'note': 'n⁺ source and drain formed in it'} and add a separate item at the top, {'label': 'Reference electrode (Ag/AgCl)', 'note': 'in the sample, completes the circuit'}, above the electrolyte layer.

problem: The layer is labelled 'Gate oxide (Ta₂O₅)'. Section 1 correctly describes the stack as a thin SiO₂ gate oxide plus a deposited Si₃N₄ or Ta₂O₅ sensing layer. Ta₂O₅ is not the gate oxide; it is the top sensing dielectric that carries the SiOH/TaOH sites.
fix: Label it 'Gate insulator / sensing layer (Si₃N₄ or Ta₂O₅)' with note 'surface charge sites', and keep the SiO₂ gate oxide as the layer under it.

problem: ΔpH is written as 7.4 − 7.1 = 0.3, i.e. initial minus final. By convention Δ means final minus initial, so ΔpH should be −0.3 here; the sign of ΔV_G then contradicts step 2 unless the reader guesses the convention.
fix: Write ΔpH = 7.1 − 7.4 = −0.3 pH units, then |ΔV_G| = 59.16 mV/pH × 0.3 pH = 17.7 mV, and state the direction separately: pH falling raises the surface potential, so the feedback gate moves down by 17.7 mV and I_D at fixed V_G rises.

problem: 'The gate window is the only exposed silicon area' is wrong. Silicon is never exposed; the window opens onto the gate insulator (oxide or nitride), which contacts the sample.
fix: Say: the gate window is the only place where the gate insulator touches the sample; everything else is sealed by epoxy, polyimide or nitride.

problem: 'That potential is in series with the gate capacitance' is loose. The surface potential adds in series with the applied gate voltage; the double-layer capacitance at the electrolyte interface sits in series with the gate capacitance and forms a voltage divider with it.
fix: Say: the surface potential adds in series with the applied gate voltage, and the electrolyte double-layer capacitance divides with the gate capacitance, so only part of the surface potential appears across the channel and shifts V_T.

problem: The step list grows SiO₂ and then jumps to lithography, but the sensing nitride or Ta₂O₅ layer named in section 1 is never deposited. A student following the steps cannot build the stack the chapter describes.
fix: Add a step after oxidation: deposit the Si₃N₄ (LPCVD) or Ta₂O₅ sensing layer on the gate oxide before photolithography defines the gate windows.

problem: The estimate 'one electronic charge gives a sub-millivolt surface-potential change' is quoted without its dependence on gate capacitance, and the exponent is printed as '10−19', which reads as a subtraction.
fix: Write q = 1.602×10<sup>−19</sup> C, note ΔV = q/C, and give the value for a stated size, e.g. for a 10 µm × 10 µm gate with 10 nm oxide, C ≈ 0.35 pF so ΔV ≈ 0.5 µV; smaller gates give larger shifts, up to a few millivolts for nanoscale devices.
